messages:
maya: hey -- first-week onboarding q: what's the fastest path to get Vault secrets + KMS key access for a new service I'm standing up? also: any rotation basics I should know now? cc @kim

kim (DevEx): welcome, maya! :tada: quick checklist —
1) join the `vault-users` GitHub team (request via org invite)
2) submit the secrets access form: https://go.redwood.internal/forms/secrets-request (choose 'new-service')
3) if you need a KMS key, pick the env + key-type (symmetric/asymmetric) in the form. infra will provision + approve.

Common commands for testing once you have access:
```bash
vault login -method=oidc
vault kv get secret/data/redwood/<service-name>
```
(Do not paste creds in public channels)

devex-bot: Welcome Maya! Your onboarding checklist item "Vault access requested" was added to your profile. :white_check_mark:

infra-ops: FYI on the KMS side: include the key alias, intended use (signing/encryption), and which env (dev/staging/prod). Our provisioning requires justification for prod keys and a rotation window. Template snippet for the ticket: `env, service, reason, rotation_days, owner_email`.

louise (Security): Rotation basics: user credentials rotate every 90 days by default. Service-level long-lived keys are discouraged; prefer short-lived tokens or workload identity. If you absolutely need a long-lived key (rare), security approval is required and we set up automated rotation with IAM hooks. Exceptions go to security@redwood.com.

samir: If you need something immediately for smoke tests I can issue a short-lived token (24h) — tell me the service name and which secrets you need.

maya: thanks all! submitting the form now. sign-off question: who is the approver chain for secrets requests? manager + security?

kim (DevEx): yep — requester -> owning team lead -> security or infra depending on request type. Expect ~1 business day for dev/staging, longer for prod keys. If it's blocking a demo, add "expedite" and tag @samir. :+1:

maya: perfect, appreciated!
